Title: RG-001 — Scaffold the resume-generator monorepo
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 is a single Python folder with a Streamlit entrypoint. v2 has a web app, an API,
a compile service, and shared packages that must version together.

**Outcome.** A new `resume-generator` repo where `pnpm dev` starts the web app and API together,
and every subsequent ticket has an obvious place to put its files.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `pnpm install && pnpm dev` boots Next.js on :3000 and FastAPI on :8000 from a clean checkout.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` each run across every workspace and pass.
- `README.md` gets a new engineer running in under ten minutes with no tribal knowledge.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
package.json                pnpm workspaces, scripts: dev, build, lint, typecheck, test, ds:sync
pnpm-workspace.yaml         apps/*, packages/*
turbo.json                  task graph + caching
.nvmrc                      22
apps/web/                   create-next-app: TS, App Router, no Tailwind, src dir, ESLint
apps/api/pyproject.toml     uv project, Python 3.12, deps: fastapi uvicorn[standard] pydantic-settings
                            supabase langgraph langgraph-checkpoint-postgres httpx anthropic openai
apps/api/resume_api/__init__.py
apps/api/Makefile           dev, test, lint targets
packages/tokens/            placeholder, filled by RG-010
packages/ui/                placeholder, filled by RG-011
packages/contracts/         placeholder, filled by RG-004
services/latex/             placeholder, filled by RG-035
supabase/                   placeholder, filled by RG-002
.github/workflows/ci.yml    placeholder, filled by RG-008
AGENTS.md                   implementation rules (copy the "Rules" section of plan/README.md)
.env.example                every var any workspace reads, with a comment per line
```

### Steps
1. `pnpm create next-app@latest apps/web --ts --app --src-dir --eslint --no-tailwind --import-alias "@/*"`.
   Tailwind is deliberately off — styling is token-based CSS Modules (ADR-002).
2. Add Turborepo; declare `build` depends on `^build`, and cache `lint`/`typecheck`/`test`.
3. `uv init apps/api` with the dep list above. Add `ruff` + `mypy` (strict on `resume_api`) + `pytest`.
4. Root `dev` script uses `concurrently` to run `turbo dev --filter=web` and `make -C apps/api dev`.
5. Wire `pnpm lint/typecheck/test` to fan out to both ecosystems (turbo for JS, make for Python).
6. Write `AGENTS.md`: no unlisted files, tokens only for visual values, tests ship with the ticket,
   reuse v1 where `plan/01-v1-reuse-map.md` says to.
7. Commit `plan/` into the new repo so implementing models can read their own tickets.

### Tests
- CI-equivalent smoke: fresh clone → install → `pnpm build` succeeds.
- `apps/api`: one `test_smoke.py` asserting the package imports.

### Definition of done
Clean clone to running dev environment in one documented command. No TODOs in `.env.example`.

### Out of scope
Deployment, Docker Compose for the full stack (RG-008), any product code.

Title: RG-002 — Supabase schema, migrations, and RLS
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 stores everything on the local filesystem under `companies/<company>/<role>/`,
keyed by nothing but a path. Two users would overwrite each other. Application status lives in a
loose `application_status.json`.

**Outcome.** Every piece of a user's data — applications, runs, templates, prompts, source of
truth, keys — is a row that belongs to exactly one user and is unreachable by any other.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A signed-in user can only ever read or write rows where `user_id = auth.uid()`, enforced by the
  database itself, not by application code.
- The schema can represent every field v1 persisted in `review.json` and `application_status.json`.
- Migrations run forward on an empty database with no manual steps.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
supabase/config.toml
supabase/migrations/0001_extensions.sql       pgcrypto, uuid-ossp
supabase/migrations/0002_profiles.sql
supabase/migrations/0003_source_of_truth.sql
supabase/migrations/0004_templates.sql
supabase/migrations/0005_prompts.sql
supabase/migrations/0006_applications.sql
supabase/migrations/0007_runs.sql
supabase/migrations/0008_documents.sql
supabase/migrations/0009_api_keys.sql
supabase/migrations/0010_rls.sql              one policy set per table
supabase/seed/                                system-default prompts + templates (RG-021, RG-022)
apps/api/resume_api/db.py                     supabase client factory, per-request user-scoped
```

### Schema

`profiles` — `id uuid pk references auth.users`, `email citext unique`, `full_name`,
`theme text default 'system'`, `default_generation_model`, `default_review_model`,
`default_revision_model`, `max_revisions int default 1`, `resume_pass_score numeric default 8.0`,
`ats_pass_threshold int default 80`, timestamps.

`allowed_emails` — `email citext pk`, `invited_at`, `invited_by`, `redeemed_at`. No RLS; service
role only. Gates sign-in (RG-003).

`sot_companies` — user_id, name, role_title, start_date, end_date, location, sort_order.
`sot_projects` — user_id, company_id fk, name, summary, tech text[].
`sot_bullets` — user_id, company_id fk, project_id fk null, text, metrics text[], tags text[].
`sot_skills` — user_id, name citext, category, proficiency, years numeric,
`evidence_bullet_ids uuid[]`. Unique `(user_id, lower(name))`.

The split matters: the evidence gate (RG-036) needs to point a keyword at a *specific* company
or project **and** a *specific* bullet. v1's flat `source_of_truth.txt` cannot express that.

`templates` — user_id null-for-system, key, name, kind `('single_page','multi_page')`,
tex_source text, storage_path text null, is_system bool, derived_from uuid null, timestamps.

`prompts` — user_id null-for-system, stage enum
`('targeting','generation','review','revision','ats','cover_letter')`, body text, version int,
is_active bool. Unique `(user_id, stage, version)`. System rows have `user_id is null`.

`applications` — user_id, company_name, company_slug, job_title, role_slug, jd_text,
jd_source_type `('text','url','upload')`, jd_url, source `('generated','imported')`,
status `('draft','applied','screening','interviewing','offer','rejected','withdrawn')`,
round_count int, current_round, next_action, notes, applied_at, timestamps.
Index `(user_id, updated_at desc)`; unique `(user_id, company_slug, role_slug, created_at)`.

`runs` — application_id fk, user_id, status
`('queued','running','succeeded','failed','cancelled')`, template_id fk, recommended_template_key,
template_reason, targeting_brief jsonb, resume_review jsonb, resume_score numeric,
fix_resolution_matrix jsonb, revision_count int, ats jsonb, warnings text[], compile_errors jsonb,
token_usage jsonb, cost_usd numeric, error text, started_at, finished_at.
The `ats` jsonb mirrors v1's keys exactly: `total_score, grade, keyword_score, structural_score,
semantic_score, matched, missing_required, missing_preferred, top_actions, hard_requirements,
all_hard_met, error`.

`run_events` — run_id fk, seq int, node text, status, payload jsonb, created_at.
Unique `(run_id, seq)`. This is the SSE replay log (RG-032).

`documents` — user_id, application_id, run_id null, kind
`('resume_tex','resume_pdf','cover_letter_tex','cover_letter_pdf','jd','imported_resume')`,
storage_path, byte_size, content_hash, created_at.

`api_keys` — user_id, provider `('anthropic','openai','openrouter')`, ciphertext bytea,
last_four text, label, created_at, last_used_at. Unique `(user_id, provider, label)`.

### RLS
Enable on every table above except `allowed_emails`. Standard policy per table:
`using (user_id = auth.uid())` for select/update/delete, `with check (user_id = auth.uid())` for
insert. `templates` and `prompts` additionally allow `select` where `user_id is null` (system rows).

### Steps
1. `supabase init`; write migrations in the order above, each idempotent and forward-only.
2. Write every table with `created_at timestamptz default now()` and a `set_updated_at` trigger.
3. Add a `handle_new_user` trigger on `auth.users` that inserts a `profiles` row and clones the
   system prompt + template rows for the new user (RG-021/022 supply the content).
4. Generate types: `supabase gen types typescript` → `packages/contracts/src/database.types.ts`.

### Reuse from v1
`slugify()` from `resume_agent/storage.py` → `apps/api/resume_api/util/slug.py`, unchanged. It
produces `company_slug`/`role_slug`. `default_application_status()` defines the status field set.

### Tests
- `supabase/tests/rls.test.sql` (pgTAP): user A cannot select, update, or delete any of user B's
  rows in every RLS-enabled table. This test is the ticket.
- Migration replay on an empty DB in CI.

### Definition of done
Migrations apply cleanly; pgTAP RLS suite green; generated TS types committed.

### Out of scope
Seed content (RG-021, RG-022), any API route.

Title: RG-003 — Google sign-in with invite-only access
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 has no concept of a user. v2 needs one identity per person, and access is
closed while the product is early.

**User story.** As an invited person I sign in with Google and land in my own workspace. As an
uninvited person I see a register-interest screen instead of an error.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Sign in with Google is the only auth method.
- An email absent from `allowed_emails` is signed straight back out and shown register-interest.
  No half-created account is left behind.
- Session survives a refresh and a server restart.
- Every API route rejects a request with no valid Supabase JWT with `401`.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/lib/supabase/client.ts        browser client
apps/web/src/lib/supabase/server.ts        RSC/route-handler client (cookie-based)
apps/web/src/middleware.ts                 session refresh + route guard
apps/web/src/app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(auth)/callback/route.ts  exchanges code, runs the allowlist check
apps/web/src/app/(auth)/no-access/page.tsx register-interest
apps/api/resume_api/auth.py                get_current_user dependency
apps/api/resume_api/middleware/auth.py
supabase/migrations/0011_allowlist_guard.sql
```

### Steps
1. Enable the Google provider in Supabase Auth; redirect URL `/(auth)/callback`.
2. In the callback route: exchange the code, read the session email, `select 1 from allowed_emails
   where email = ...`. If absent → `supabase.auth.signOut()` and redirect `/no-access`. If present
   → stamp `redeemed_at` and redirect `/pipeline`.
3. Also enforce server-side: a Postgres `before insert` trigger on `profiles` raises unless the
   email is allowlisted. The client check is UX; the trigger is the actual gate.
4. `middleware.ts`: refresh the session cookie on every request; redirect unauthenticated users
   away from `/(app)/*` to `/sign-in`.
5. API: `get_current_user` verifies the JWT against the Supabase JWKS, returns `UserContext(id,
   email)`, and is a dependency on the whole authenticated router. Never trust a `user_id` from a
   request body — it always comes from the token.
6. Register-interest form posts to `POST /public/interest` (rate-limited, unauthenticated) which
   inserts into an `interest_requests` table.

### Tests
- API: request with no token → 401; with a token for user A → `UserContext.id == A`.
- API: a request body carrying a foreign `user_id` is ignored, not honoured.
- Web (Playwright): allowlisted email reaches `/pipeline`; non-allowlisted lands on `/no-access`
  with no session cookie remaining.

### Definition of done
Both tests green; no route in `/(app)` renders for an anonymous visitor.

### Out of scope
Admin UI for issuing invites (RG-051). Seed the first cohort with SQL.

Title: RG-004 — FastAPI application skeleton and API contract
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** Every later API ticket will otherwise re-invent error shapes, pagination, and
settings loading, and the web app will hand-write fetch calls that drift from the server.

**Outcome.** One consistent, typed API surface; the web client is generated from it, so a
breaking server change fails the web typecheck.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every error response has the same JSON shape.
- `/docs` describes every route accurately.
- The web app imports a generated client; no hand-written `fetch` to the API anywhere.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/main.py            app factory, CORS, routers, exception handlers
apps/api/resume_api/settings.py        pydantic-settings, fails fast on a missing var
apps/api/resume_api/errors.py          AppError hierarchy + handler
apps/api/resume_api/schemas/common.py  Page[T], ErrorBody, IdResponse
apps/api/resume_api/routers/health.py
apps/api/resume_api/deps.py            db session, current user, blob store
packages/contracts/package.json        openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch
packages/contracts/src/client.ts       typed client factory
scripts/gen-contracts.sh               boots the API, dumps openapi.json, generates TS
```

### Contracts
Error envelope, used by every failure path:
```json
{ "error": { "code": "run_budget_exceeded", "message": "Human sentence.", "details": {} } }
```
`code` is a stable snake_case string the UI can switch on. `message` follows the arey voice:
what happened, then what to do, no exclamation marks.

List responses: `{ "items": [...], "next_cursor": null }`. Cursor pagination, never offset.

### Steps
1. App factory with routers mounted under `/v1`. CORS allows only the web origin from settings.
2. `AppError(code, message, status, details)`; subclasses `NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Conflict`,
   `BudgetExceeded`, `UpstreamFailed`, `ValidationFailed`. One handler renders them all.
   A bare `Exception` handler logs with a request id and returns `internal_error` — never a stack.
3. Request-id middleware: accept or mint `X-Request-Id`, bind it to structured logs, echo it back.
4. `/v1/health` returns `{status, version, db: ok|degraded}`.
5. `scripts/gen-contracts.sh` runs in CI and fails the build if the committed client is stale.

### Tests
- Error handler: a raised `NotFound` renders the envelope with status 404.
- Settings: a missing required env var raises at import, not at first request.
- Contract freshness check runs in CI.

### Definition of done
`/docs` clean, generated client committed, CI enforces freshness.

### Out of scope
Any domain route.

Title: RG-005 — Next.js app skeleton and routing
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The v1 prototype (`Resume Agent.dc.html`) proved six screens. They need real routes,
real layouts, and real loading and error states.

**Outcome.** Every screen has a URL, a loading state, and an error state, before any of them has
content.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Deep-linking to any screen works; back and forward behave.
- Every route shows a skeleton while loading, never a blank page or a spinner-on-white.
- An API failure shows a recoverable error state with a retry, not a crashed boundary.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx                 fonts, theme attribute, tokens import
apps/web/src/app/page.tsx                   landing (RG-048)
apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx           authenticated shell (RG-013)
apps/web/src/app/(app)/pipeline/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/new/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/[id]/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/[id]/runs/[runId]/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/source-of-truth/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/templates/page.tsx
apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx
    …each with loading.tsx and error.tsx
apps/web/src/lib/api.ts                     server-side client with the auth token attached
apps/web/src/lib/query.ts                   TanStack Query provider + defaults
```

### Steps
1. Route group `(app)` carries the authenticated shell; `(auth)` and `/` do not.
2. Server components fetch through `lib/api.ts` (token from the Supabase server client).
   Client components use TanStack Query against the same generated client.
3. Query defaults: `staleTime` 30 s, one retry, no refetch-on-focus for run data (SSE owns that).
4. `loading.tsx` renders static `--bg-inset` skeleton blocks — no shimmer (ADR-002 / arey).
5. `error.tsx` renders the arey `EmptyState` pattern with the error `code` mapped to a sentence
   and a "Try again" button calling `reset()`.
6. Theme: `data-theme` on `<html>`, resolved from `profiles.theme`, with a no-flash inline script
   reading `localStorage` before paint.

### Tests
- Playwright: each route renders its heading for a signed-in user.
- A forced API 500 renders the error state, and the retry re-requests.

### Definition of done
All nine routes reachable with loading and error states; no hydration warnings in the console.

### Out of scope
Screen content (Epic E), nav chrome (RG-013).

Title: RG-006 — Document storage abstraction
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 writes `.tex`, `.pdf`, `JD.txt`, and `review.json` to a local folder tree. That is
not shareable, not backed up, and not multi-user.

**Outcome.** Documents are stored per user, downloadable by the owner and nobody else, with a
storage backend the product is not married to.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A user can download their own resume PDF; the same URL fails for anyone else.
- Download links expire.
- Swapping the storage provider touches exactly one class.

## Technical plan

Decision D1 in `plan/03-open-decisions.md`: Supabase Storage, private bucket `documents`.

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/storage/base.py        BlobStore protocol
apps/api/resume_api/storage/supabase.py    SupabaseBlobStore
apps/api/resume_api/storage/paths.py       canonical path builder
apps/api/resume_api/routers/documents.py   GET /v1/documents/{id}/url
supabase/migrations/0012_storage_bucket.sql
```

### Contracts
```python
class BlobStore(Protocol):
    async def put(self, path: str, data: bytes, content_type: str) -> str: ...
    async def get(self, path: str) -> bytes: ...
    async def signed_url(self, path: str, ttl_seconds: int = 60) -> str: ...
    async def delete(self, path: str) -> None: ...
```
Path shape: `{user_id}/{application_id}/{run_id}/{kind}.{ext}`. Built only by `paths.py` —
no string concatenation at call sites.

### Steps
1. Create the private bucket in a migration with a storage policy scoped to
   `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text`.
2. Every `put` also inserts a `documents` row (path, byte size, sha256). The row is the index;
   the bucket is the bytes. Never list the bucket to find a file.
3. `GET /v1/documents/{id}/url` checks ownership via the `documents` row, then returns a 60 s
   signed URL. PDF bytes never pass through FastAPI.

### Reuse from v1
The file *names* v1 chose (`hamsa_resume.tex`, `cover_letter.tex`, `JD.txt`, `review.json`) map to
the `documents.kind` enum. `review.json` becomes the `runs` row, not a blob.

### Tests
- Round-trip put/get/delete against a local Supabase.
- Ownership: user B requesting user A's document id gets 404 (not 403 — do not leak existence).
- A signed URL is unusable after its TTL.

### Definition of done
All three tests green; no call site imports `supabase.py` directly.

### Out of scope
PDF generation (RG-035).

Title: RG-007 — Structured logging, errors, and run telemetry
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** A generation run makes up to sixteen LLM calls across three providers. When one
fails or a run costs more than expected, there must be a record of why.

**Outcome.** Every run is reconstructable after the fact: which node, which model, how many
tokens, how long, what failed.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Any run id can be traced end to end from the logs.
- A failed run shows the user a plain sentence and the operator a full trace.
- No API key, resume body, or JD text is ever written to a log.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/logging.py       structlog JSON config, secret redaction processor
apps/api/resume_api/telemetry.py     record_llm_call(run_id, node, provider, model, usage, ms)
apps/web/src/lib/errors.ts           error code → user sentence map
```

### Steps
1. structlog to JSON on stdout. Bind `request_id`, `user_id`, `run_id` for the request's lifetime.
2. A redaction processor drops keys matching `api_key|authorization|ciphertext|tex|jd_text|
   resume_text` and truncates any string over 500 chars.
3. `record_llm_call` appends to `runs.token_usage` jsonb and increments `runs.cost_usd` using a
   static price table in `llm/pricing.py`.
4. Sentry on both apps, with the same redaction rules and `request_id` as a tag.
5. `errors.ts` maps each server `code` to arey-voice copy. Unknown codes fall back to
   "Something failed on our side. Try again in a moment."

### Tests
- The redaction processor removes each named key, verified per key.
- `record_llm_call` accumulates cost correctly over three calls.

### Definition of done
A deliberately failed run produces one traceable log chain and zero secret leaks.

### Out of scope
Dashboards, alerting.

Title: RG-008 — One-command local development environment
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The stack is five moving parts — Next.js, FastAPI, Postgres, Storage, and a LaTeX
compiler — plus three paid LLM providers. Without a scripted local environment, every
implementing model burns its first hour on setup and some of them will reach for a real API key
to run a test.

**Outcome.** `make bootstrap && pnpm dev` produces a fully working app with seeded data, on a
machine with no LaTeX, no Postgres, and no API keys.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A clean machine reaches a working, signed-in app with sample data in under ten minutes.
- The full test suite runs offline, with zero real LLM calls and zero cost.
- Compiling a resume to PDF works locally with no TeX installation.
- A single command resets the database to a known seeded state.

## Technical plan

This ticket is the reason the other 36 can be implemented cheaply. Treat developer experience
here as a product requirement, not a nicety.

### Files
```
Makefile                              bootstrap, dev, reset, seed, test, doctor
docker-compose.dev.yml                supabase stack + latex service
scripts/bootstrap.sh                  preflight checks → install → migrate → seed
scripts/doctor.sh                     diagnose a broken environment
supabase/seed/dev_seed.sql            one demo user with realistic data
apps/api/resume_api/llm/fake.py       deterministic offline LLM client
apps/api/tests/fixtures/llm/*.json    recorded responses per prompt stage
.env.development                      committed; safe non-secret local defaults
```

### The offline LLM client — the important part
`FakeLLMClient` implements the `LLMClient` protocol (RG-031) and returns recorded fixtures keyed
by `(stage, hash(prompt))`, falling back to a generic valid response for that stage. It must
return **schema-valid** output for every stage: strict JSON for targeting and review (so
`parse_strict_json_object` succeeds), compilable LaTeX for generation and revision.

`LLM_MODE=fake` is the default in `.env.development` and in CI. `LLM_MODE=live` requires real
keys and is opt-in, never the default. A test that makes a network call to a provider fails —
enforce it with a socket guard in `conftest.py`.

This is what makes RG-030's graph testable: the whole pipeline, including revision loops, runs
end to end in under two seconds with no money spent.

### Steps
1. `docker-compose.dev.yml` runs the Supabase local stack (Postgres, GoTrue, Storage, Kong) and
   the RG-035 LaTeX container. Nothing else needs Docker.
2. `make bootstrap`: check versions (Node 22, pnpm, uv, Python 3.12, Docker) and print a specific
   fix for each missing one → `pnpm install` → `uv sync` → start compose → apply migrations →
   seed system prompts and templates → seed the demo user.
3. `dev_seed.sql` creates `dev@localhost` in `allowed_emails` and `auth.users` with a known
   password, a populated source of truth derived from `base/source_of_truth.txt`, three
   applications in different statuses, and one completed run with real scores. A seeded app that
   looks like a used app is worth an hour of manual clicking on every ticket in Epic E.
4. Local sign-in bypass: when `AUTH_MODE=local`, a "Sign in as dev@localhost" button appears on
   the sign-in page. It is compiled out entirely unless `NODE_ENV === 'development'` — assert that
   with a test, because an auth bypass reaching production is the worst possible outcome of this
   ticket.
5. `make reset` drops, re-migrates, and re-seeds. `make doctor` reports which of the five services
   is unhealthy and how to fix it.
6. `README.md` gets a "Getting started" section that is exactly these commands and nothing else.

### Tests
- CI runs `scripts/bootstrap.sh` on a clean runner and asserts the app answers on both ports.
- The socket guard: a test attempting a real provider call fails with a clear message.
- A full pipeline run completes in fake mode in under 5 s, with the same node sequence as live.
- The dev sign-in bypass is absent from a production build (assert against the built bundle).

### Definition of done
Four tests green; a second machine bootstraps from the README with no undocumented steps.

### Out of scope
Cloud environments (RG-054).

Title: RG-009 — Continuous integration and quality gates
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** A single-maintainer project with small models writing code needs the pipeline, not
the reviewer, to catch mistakes.

**Outcome.** Nothing merges that fails lint, types, tests, migrations, or the contract freshness
check. Merging to `main` deploys.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A PR that breaks the API contract fails CI with a message naming the drift.
- A PR touching `supabase/migrations` runs them against a throwaway database.
- Every gate runs offline in fake-LLM mode (RG-008) — CI never spends money.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
.github/workflows/ci.yml         lint, typecheck, test, migrate, contracts, bootstrap
apps/api/Dockerfile
services/latex/Dockerfile
```

### Steps
1. CI jobs: `web` (eslint, tsc, vitest, playwright), `api` (ruff, mypy strict, pytest),
   `db` (spin Postgres, apply migrations, run the pgTAP RLS suite from RG-002),
   `contracts` (regenerate and `git diff --exit-code`).
2. A `bootstrap` job runs `scripts/bootstrap.sh` (RG-008) on a clean runner and smoke-tests both ports.
3. `LLM_MODE=fake` is forced in CI, and the socket guard from RG-008 fails any test that reaches a provider.
4. Images for `apps/api` and `services/latex` build on every PR so a broken Dockerfile is caught before RG-054 needs it.

### Tests
CI is the test. Add one deliberately-broken branch to prove each gate fires, then delete it.

### Definition of done
Green pipeline on `main`; every gate proven to fire once.

### Out of scope
Deployment and cloud environments — RG-054.

Title: RG-010 — Design token pipeline from the external design-system repo
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The arey design system lives in a separate GitHub repo with no build step and no
package. Copying values into the app guarantees drift; importing its JSX directly is not
buildable in Next.js.

**Outcome.** Token changes made in the design-system repo reach the product in one command, and
it is impossible to commit a hard-coded colour, radius, shadow, or duration.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `pnpm ds:sync` updates tokens from a pinned upstream commit and reports what changed.
- A PR introducing `#0071e3` or `border-radius: 12px` in app code fails lint.
- Light and dark themes both switch entirely via `data-theme`, with no component-level branching.

## Technical plan

Implements ADR-002 (`plan/02-design-system-strategy.md`) — the *consume* half.

### Files
```
packages/tokens/upstream.json          { repo, ref (commit SHA), paths[] }
packages/tokens/scripts/sync.ts        fetch → write → verify
packages/tokens/css/                   generated: fonts, colors, typography, spacing, radius,
                                       elevation, motion, base  (DO NOT EDIT header on each)
packages/tokens/src/index.ts           export const tokens = {...} as const  (name → var())
packages/tokens/src/types.ts           type TokenName = '--accent-solid' | …  (generated)
packages/tokens/PARITY.md              upstream SHA + sync date log
eslint-config/no-raw-design-values.js  custom rule
```

### Steps
1. `sync.ts` fetches the eight `tokens/*.css` files plus `styles.css` at the pinned SHA, writes
   them into `packages/tokens/css/` with a generated-file banner, and parses every
   `--custom-property` declaration into the TS union and the `tokens` object.
2. **Removal guard:** after generating, scan `packages/ui/**` and `apps/web/**` for `var(--x)`
   usages. If a used token no longer exists upstream, exit non-zero and list them. Bumping the
   pin must be a deliberate, reviewed PR.
3. `apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx` imports `@repo/tokens/css/index.css` once, globally. This is the
   only global stylesheet in the app.
4. Custom ESLint rule `no-raw-design-values`: error on hex colours, `rgb()`/`hsl()` literals,
   `px` radii, `box-shadow` literals, `transition` durations, and font-family strings inside
   `.module.css` and inline `style` props. Allowed: `0`, `1px` hairlines, `100%`, `var(...)`.
5. Fonts: Instrument Sans + JetBrains Mono via `next/font`, exposed as `--font-sans`/`--font-mono`
   so the upstream `fonts.css` contract still holds without a network font request.

### Tests
- `sync.ts` against a fixture: known input CSS produces the expected union and object.
- Removal guard fires when a referenced token is deleted from the fixture.
- ESLint rule: fixture file with a hex colour errors; the same file using `var(--accent-solid)` passes.

### Definition of done
Tokens generated and committed, pin recorded, lint rule active in CI.

### Out of scope
Components (RG-011).

Title: RG-011 — Rebuild arey primitives as typed React components
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The upstream components are preview-environment JSX: untyped, not RSC-safe, no
tree-shaking, no tests. The product needs the same visual language as real, typed components.

**Outcome.** Every screen in Epic E is assembled from `@repo/ui` and adds no bespoke styling.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Each component matches its upstream counterpart's anatomy and every interaction state
  (hover, press, focus-visible, disabled, selected).
- Every visual value in `packages/ui` is a `var(--*)` reference. Zero literals.
- Keyboard operation and `prefers-reduced-motion` work on every interactive component.

## Technical plan

Implements ADR-002 — the *rebuild* half. Upstream JSX is the **spec**; do not copy it verbatim.

### Files
```
packages/ui/src/core/{Button,IconButton,Icon,Card,Badge,Tag,Kbd,Avatar}.tsx
packages/ui/src/forms/{Input,Textarea,Select,Checkbox,Radio,Switch,Field}.tsx
packages/ui/src/feedback/{Dialog,Toast,Tooltip,Spinner,ProgressBar,EmptyState}.tsx
packages/ui/src/navigation/{Tabs,SegmentedControl,Breadcrumbs,SidebarNav,ListRow}.tsx
packages/ui/src/**/<Name>.module.css
packages/ui/PARITY.md                upstream path → our file → verified SHA → deviations
packages/ui/src/index.ts
```

### Rules (from the arey guide — non-negotiable)
- Sentence case on every label. No emoji, ever. No unicode glyphs standing in for icons.
- Machine-produced values (durations, scores, SHAs, timestamps, percentages in tables) use
  `--font-mono`.
- Cards: `--surface-card`, `--radius-card`, **hairline border and soft shadow, both**.
- Glass (`--surface-glass` + `--backdrop-glass`) only on floating layers: top bar, popovers,
  dialogs, toasts. Never on a static card.
- Press = `transform: scale(var(--press-scale))`. Focus = `--ring-focus`, `:focus-visible` only,
  replacing hover. Disabled = `opacity: .4` and nothing else.
- Radii nest downward: 16px card → 12px control → 6px inner chip.
- No left-border accent stripes. One accent colour only.
- `Icon` wraps the Phosphor web font; never a raw `<i>`. Regular by default, Fill only for
  selected state, Bold only at 12–14px.

### Steps
1. For each component: read the upstream file, list its props and states in `PARITY.md`, then
   implement with CSS Modules + tokens. Server-component-safe by default; `'use client'` only on
   components with state or refs (Dialog, Toast, Tooltip, Tabs, Switch, Select).
2. Dialog and Tooltip build on Radix primitives for focus trap and positioning, styled entirely
   by our CSS Modules. Do not re-implement focus management.
3. Motion: entries are opacity + `translateY(4–8px)` + `scale(.98→1)` over 220ms with
   `--ease-out`. Interactive feedback 140ms with `--ease-spring`.
   `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroes every duration and the press scale.
4. Ship a Storybook (or a `/kitchen-sink` route, if Storybook is too much weight) with every
   component in every state, light and dark.

### Tests
- `vitest` + Testing Library per component: renders, prop variants, disabled blocks the handler.
- `jest-axe` on every component; zero violations.
- A repo-wide test asserting no literal hex or px-radius appears in `packages/ui/**/*.module.css`.
- Playwright visual snapshots of the kitchen sink in both themes.

### Definition of done
All 27 components shipped with a `PARITY.md` row each; a11y and token tests green.

### Out of scope
App-specific composites — ScoreDial, ATSKeywordList, RunTimeline — which belong to their
feature tickets in Epic E.

Title: RG-012 — Theming, dark mode, and responsive foundations
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The v1 prototype has a working light/dark toggle and a 940px responsive break. Both
have to be real, persisted, and flash-free.

**User story.** I set dark mode once and every device I sign in on respects it, with no white
flash on load.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Three theme choices: light, dark, system. Persisted to the profile, not just the browser.
- No flash of the wrong theme on first paint, including on a hard refresh.
- Every layout works from 360px to 1920px with no horizontal scroll.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/lib/theme.tsx                 provider + useTheme
apps/web/src/app/theme-script.tsx          blocking inline script
apps/web/src/styles/breakpoints.ts         sm 600, md 940, lg 1200, xl 1440
apps/api/resume_api/routers/profile.py     PATCH /v1/profile { theme }
```

### Steps
1. Inline script in `<head>` reads `localStorage.theme` (or `matchMedia`) and sets
   `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` before paint. It is the only blocking script.
2. `useTheme().set(t)` writes localStorage, updates the attribute, and fires `PATCH /v1/profile`
   optimistically. On sign-in the server value seeds localStorage.
3. Theme transition is opacity-only at 80ms per the arey guide — never a colour transition on
   every element.
4. **940px is the shell breakpoint** (matching the v1 prototype): above, a persistent 264px
   sidebar; below, a glass top bar with a hamburger opening a sheet. RG-013 implements the chrome;
   this ticket owns the token and the media-query helper.
5. Content caps: `--content-max` 1120px centred; prose at `--prose-max` 68ch.

### Tests
- Playwright: set dark, hard reload, assert the first painted frame is dark (no flash).
- Theme persists across sign-out and sign-in on a second browser context.
- Viewport sweep at 360/600/940/1200/1920 — no horizontal overflow on any route.

### Definition of done
All three tests green.

### Out of scope
Nav chrome (RG-013).

Title: RG-013 — Authenticated app shell
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** Six screens need one consistent frame: where am I, how do I get elsewhere, who am I
signed in as, and how do I start a new application from anywhere.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The active screen is unmistakable in the nav.
- "New application" is reachable in one click from every screen.
- Under 940px the sidebar becomes a hamburger sheet; nothing is unreachable at 360px.
- A run in progress shows a persistent indicator in the shell, on any screen.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/components/shell/AppShell.tsx
apps/web/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx        264px, independent scroll, 24px bottom mask
apps/web/src/components/shell/TopBar.tsx         56px sticky, glass
apps/web/src/components/shell/MobileNav.tsx      hamburger → sheet, <940px
apps/web/src/components/shell/UserMenu.tsx       avatar → popover: theme, settings, sign out
apps/web/src/components/shell/ActiveRunBadge.tsx subscribes to the in-flight run (RG-032)
```

### Structure
Sidebar sections, in order: **Pipeline**, **New application** (primary Button, not a nav row),
then a divider, then **Source of truth**, **Templates**, **Settings**. The arey wordmark
(`assets/logo.svg`, `currentColor` stroke) sits at the top; a lowercase `arey` text lockup is
used below the size at which the sketch stays legible.

### Steps
1. `AppShell` is a server component; only `MobileNav`, `UserMenu`, and `ActiveRunBadge` are client.
2. Active state from `usePathname()`: `--bg-selected` fill + `--text-accent` label. No left stripe.
3. Top bar is `position: sticky` with glass — the glass **is** the scroll protection; no gradient
   fade. The sidebar's long list gets the 24px bottom gradient mask.
4. A 1px indeterminate accent bar sits under the top bar during route transitions and while a run
   is active — the arey loading pattern. No skeleton shimmer.
5. Below 940px: hamburger opens a left sheet (`--radius-sheet`, glass, focus-trapped, Escape and
   backdrop close, focus returns to the trigger). Nav rows are ≥44px tall.
6. `ActiveRunBadge` shows `company · role` and the current node name, and links to the run page.
   It is the reason a user can navigate away from a generation and come back.

### Tests
- Playwright: nav to each route marks exactly one row active.
- At 900px the sidebar is absent and the hamburger opens a focus-trapped sheet; Escape closes it
  and returns focus.
- With a mocked in-flight run, the badge appears on the settings screen and links correctly.
- `jest-axe` on the shell: zero violations; skip-to-content link present.

### Definition of done
All four tests green at 360, 940, and 1440px.

### Out of scope
Screen content.

Title: RG-020 — Source of truth: structured model and API
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 reads a single flat file, `base/source_of_truth.txt`, and injects it wholesale
into every prompt. It works for one person, but nothing can *reference* a fact inside it — which
is exactly what the ATS evidence gate (RG-036) needs, and it cannot be edited safely by a user.

**User story.** As a user I keep one structured record of my career — companies, projects,
bullets, skills — and every generated resume is built only from facts in it.

**Acceptance criteria**
- I can add, edit, reorder, and delete companies, projects, bullets, and skills.
- A skill can be linked to the specific bullets that prove it.
- The whole record renders back to the plain-text block the prompts expect, byte-stably.
- Nothing is ever deleted silently: deleting a company warns about the bullets it owns.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/schemas/sot.py
apps/api/resume_api/repositories/sot.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/sot.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/sot_render.py     structured rows → prompt text block
apps/api/tests/test_sot_render.py
```

### Routes
```
GET    /v1/source-of-truth                 full tree (companies → projects → bullets) + skills
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/companies       PATCH/DELETE /{id}
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/projects        PATCH/DELETE /{id}
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/bullets         PATCH/DELETE /{id}
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/skills          PATCH/DELETE /{id}
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/reorder         { entity, ids[] }  → bulk sort_order write
GET    /v1/source-of-truth/rendered        the exact text the pipeline injects
POST   /v1/source-of-truth/import          paste a v1-style text block → parsed draft (no write)
```

### `sot_render.py` — the important part
The pipeline prompts (`generator.md`, `targeting_brief.md`, `reviewer.md`, `reviser.md`,
`cover_letter.md`) all take a `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` string. This function is the single producer of
that string. Deterministic ordering (company sort_order, then project sort_order, then bullet
sort_order) so identical data always yields an identical prompt — otherwise prompt caching and
run comparison both break.

Format: keep v1's shape so the existing prompts need no edits — company header line, role and
dates, then indented bullets, then a skills block grouped by category.

### Reuse from v1
- `base/source_of_truth.txt` is the reference content and the format spec. Read it, match the
  rendered output to it, and use it as the golden fixture for the render test.
- The v1 prompts consume this string unchanged. Do not change the format to "improve" it.

### Tests
- Golden test: the seeded structured record renders **byte-identical** to a fixture derived from
  `base/source_of_truth.txt`. This is the ticket's core test.
- Ordering is stable across two calls with rows inserted out of order.
- `/import` parses the v1 text block into the correct company/project/bullet counts.
- Deleting a company cascades to its projects and bullets, and returns the count it removed.

### Definition of done
Golden render test green; all CRUD routes covered; RLS verified for a second user.

### Out of scope
The editor UI (RG-045).

Title: RG-021 — LaTeX template library
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 hard-codes five template paths in `config.py` and picks between them with a
keyword heuristic. Users cannot add their own, and the ten `.tex` files that exist are invisible
to the product.

**User story.** As a user I keep a library of resume templates — the seeded defaults plus my own,
added by upload, paste, or by copying an existing one — and I choose or accept a recommendation
for each application.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Ten system templates are available on first sign-in without me doing anything.
- I can add a template three ways: upload a `.tex` file, paste LaTeX, or duplicate an existing one.
- I can rename and delete my own templates but never the system ones.
- The system still recommends a template from the job description, and tells me why.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/schemas/templates.py
apps/api/resume_api/repositories/templates.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/templates.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/template_select.py     ported from v1
apps/api/resume_api/latex/validate.py               structural sanity + safety scan
supabase/seed/templates/*.tex                       the ten v1 templates
supabase/migrations/0013_seed_templates.sql
```

### Routes
```
GET    /v1/templates                      system + mine
POST   /v1/templates                      { name, kind, tex_source } | multipart upload
POST   /v1/templates/{id}/duplicate       { name }
PATCH  /v1/templates/{id}                 own rows only
DELETE /v1/templates/{id}                 own rows only; 409 if referenced by a run
POST   /v1/templates/recommend            { jd_text, job_title } → { key, reason, alternatives[] }
```

### Steps
1. Seed: import `single_page/*.tex` (5) and `multi_page/*.tex` (5) as `is_system = true`,
   `user_id = null`, with keys `frontend, backend-java, backend-python, fullstack, senior-engineer`
   under each `kind`. Store the source in the `tex_source` column — these are small text files;
   Storage is for generated output, not for the library.
2. `validate.py` runs on every write: must contain `\documentclass` and `\begin{document}`;
   reject `\write18`, `\input{/`, `\openout`, `\immediate\write`; cap at 200 KB. Return a
   `validation_failed` error listing every problem found, not just the first.
3. `template_select.py` is v1's `resume_selection.recommend_template` moved across. Change only
   what is necessary: it returns a template **key**, which the caller resolves to the user's row
   for that key (preferring their own override of a system key).
4. Deletion is blocked while any `runs` row references the template — return `409 conflict` with
   the count, per the arey voice ("Used by 3 applications. Duplicate it instead.").

### Reuse from v1
- `resume_agent/resume_selection.py` — lift, keep its tests.
- `config.py TEMPLATE_FILES` — the key naming contract.
- `single_page/*.tex`, `multi_page/*.tex` — the seed content.

### Tests
- Port `tests/test_resume_selection.py` unchanged apart from imports. It must still pass.
- Validation rejects each unsafe macro; the error lists all of them.
- Duplicating a system template creates a user-owned copy with `derived_from` set.
- Deleting a referenced template returns 409.

### Definition of done
Ten templates seeded; the ported selection test green; validation covered.

### Out of scope
The templates UI (RG-046), compilation (RG-035).

Title: RG-022 — User-editable prompts for the six run stages
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1's prompts are five markdown files on disk. They are the product's real
intelligence, and a user who wants a different reviewing standard cannot change them.

**User story.** As a user I read and edit the prompt used at each of the six stages — targeting,
generation, review, revision, ATS, cover letter — and I can always get back to the default.

**Acceptance criteria**
- All six prompts are visible, editable, and versioned.
- Saving creates a new version; I can view history and restore any earlier version.
- "Reset to default" restores the system prompt without losing my history.
- A prompt that drops a required variable cannot be saved.
- A run records which prompt version it used.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/schemas/prompts.py
apps/api/resume_api/repositories/prompts.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/prompts.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/prompts.py        render_prompt, ported from v1
supabase/seed/prompts/{targeting,generation,review,revision,ats,cover_letter}.md
supabase/migrations/0014_seed_prompts.sql
```

### Required variables per stage (validation contract)
Taken from the actual `render_prompt` call sites in v1 `graph.py`:

| Stage | Required `{{VARS}}` |
| --- | --- |
| targeting | COMPANY_NAME, JOB_TITLE, JD_TEXT, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH |
| generation | TARGETING_BRIEF, JD_TEXT, BASE_RESUME_TEX, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH |
| review | COMPANY_NAME, JOB_TITLE, REVISION_COUNT, TARGETING_BRIEF, JD_TEXT, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, PREVIOUS_MUST_FIX, RESUME_TEX |
| revision | COMPANY_NAME, JOB_TITLE, TARGETING_BRIEF, JD_TEXT, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, RESUME_TEX, RESUME_MUST_FIX, FIX_RESOLUTION_MATRIX, RESUME_SCORE, RESUME_TARGET_SCORE, RESUME_CATEGORY_SCORES, ATS_TOP_ACTIONS, ATS_UNMET_HARD_REQUIREMENTS |
| cover_letter | COMPANY_NAME, JOB_TITLE, TARGETING_BRIEF, JD_TEXT, RESUME_TEX, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, FIX_RESOLUTION_SUMMARY |
| ats | (new in v2 — the ATS stage is deterministic in v1; this prompt only shapes the LLM's *explanation* of ATS findings, vars: JD_TEXT, ATS_FINDINGS) |

### Routes
```
GET    /v1/prompts                        active prompt per stage, with is_customised
GET    /v1/prompts/{stage}/versions
POST   /v1/prompts/{stage}                { body } → new version, becomes active
POST   /v1/prompts/{stage}/restore        { version }
POST   /v1/prompts/{stage}/reset          back to the system default
POST   /v1/prompts/{stage}/validate       dry-run the variable check
```

### Steps
1. Seed the five v1 prompt files verbatim as `user_id = null, version = 1` rows. Do not reword them.
2. `render_prompt` keeps v1's `{{VAR}}` substitution semantics exactly. It now takes a body string
   rather than a filename, and raises `ValidationFailed` on an unfilled variable at render time.
3. Validation on save: extract `{{...}}` tokens from the body, diff against the required set for
   that stage. Missing required → reject, naming each. Unknown extra token → reject (it would
   render empty and silently degrade the prompt).
4. Resolution order at run time: the user's active version for the stage, else the system row.
   The chosen `prompt_id`+`version` per stage is written into `runs.token_usage.prompts`.

### Reuse from v1
`resume_agent/prompts/*.md` (all five, verbatim), `prompt_loader.render_prompt` and
`distill_governance_prompt` (the governance/system prompt derived from
`base/resume-proj-instructions.txt` — keep it; it is what stops fabrication).

### Tests
- Every seeded prompt passes its own variable validation.
- Saving a prompt missing `{{JD_TEXT}}` is rejected and names it.
- Restore brings back an exact earlier body.
- Reset leaves version history intact.

### Definition of done
Six stages seeded and validating; a run records its prompt versions.

### Out of scope
The prompt editor UI (RG-045).

Title: RG-023 — BYOK provider keys
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `.env` — a single operator's
keys. v2 is bring-your-own-key: each user pays for their own runs.

**User story.** As a user I add my Anthropic and OpenAI keys once, see only the last four
characters afterwards, and can rotate or revoke them at any time.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A key is never returned by any API response after it is saved, in any form.
- A key is encrypted at rest with a key the database alone does not hold.
- Starting a run without the required provider key gives a clear, actionable message naming the
  provider — not a 500 from the LLM SDK.
- I can test a key before saving it.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/crypto.py               envelope encryption helpers
apps/api/resume_api/repositories/keys.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/keys.py
apps/api/resume_api/llm/credentials.py      resolve keys for a run
```

### Routes
```
GET    /v1/keys                 [{ provider, label, last_four, created_at, last_used_at }]
POST   /v1/keys                 { provider, label, secret } → 201, body has no secret
POST   /v1/keys/test            { provider, secret } → { ok, model_count } — never persists
DELETE /v1/keys/{id}
```

### Steps
1. Encrypt with AES-256-GCM using a data key derived per user from a master key held in the API's
   secret store (never in Postgres). Store `ciphertext = nonce || tag || payload` as bytea.
   `crypto.py` exposes only `seal(user_id, plaintext)` / `open(user_id, ciphertext)`.
2. Decryption happens once per run, in memory, inside the pipeline process. Keys are never bound
   to a log context, never in an exception message, never in `runs` jsonb. The RG-007 redaction
   processor is the second line of defence, not the first.
3. `POST /v1/keys/test` calls the provider's cheapest metadata endpoint (`GET /v1/models`) and
   returns only `ok` and a count.
4. Preflight in the run creator (RG-032): resolve every provider the selected models require; if
   one is missing return `400 missing_api_key` with `details.provider`. The UI deep-links to
   settings from that code.

### Tests
- `seal`/`open` round-trips; a ciphertext sealed for user A fails to open for user B.
- No response schema in the OpenAPI document contains a `secret` field — assert this in a test
  that walks the generated schema.
- A run started without the needed key returns `missing_api_key`, and no LLM call is attempted.
- Redaction test: force an exception carrying a key; assert it is absent from the log output.

### Definition of done
All four tests green; a security note in the README explaining the threat model plainly.

### Out of scope
Billing, usage limits per key, org-shared keys.

Title: RG-030 — Port the LangGraph pipeline to the API
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The generation pipeline is the product. It works today in v1 and must not regress
while moving off Streamlit.

**Outcome.** The same graph, the same nodes, the same termination behaviour — running inside
FastAPI, per user, against database-backed inputs.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The node sequence is unchanged from v1 and observable in a run's event log.
- Every v1 pipeline test passes against the ported code with import-path changes only.
- Two users running simultaneously never see each other's state.

## Technical plan

This is a **port, not a rewrite**. Do not restructure the graph, rename nodes, or "simplify" the
routing. Read `plan/01-v1-reuse-map.md` before starting.

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/state.py       ← v1 resume_agent/state.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/graph.py       ← v1 resume_agent/graph.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/budgets.py     ← v1 config.py MAX_* constants
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/jd_loader.py   ← v1 jd_loader.py
apps/api/tests/pipeline/                    ← v1 tests/, ported
```

### The graph, unchanged
```
START → resolve_jd_input →(stop if no JD)→ load_inputs → create_targeting_brief
      → generate_resume → review_documents → ats_check_resume
      →(revise)→ revise_documents → review_documents   (loop)
      →(persist)→ generate_cover_letter → persist_outputs → compile_pdfs → END
```

### What changes, and only this
1. **Checkpointer.** `make_sqlite_checkpointer` → `AsyncPostgresSaver` against Supabase, with
   `thread_id = run_id`. v1's own comment already calls for this. Delete the SQLite path entirely.
2. **Input loading.** `load_inputs` no longer reads files. It takes a `RunInputs` dataclass
   assembled by the caller: rendered source of truth (RG-020), governance prompt, template
   `tex_source` (RG-021), and the six resolved prompt bodies (RG-022).
3. **Persistence.** `persist_outputs` writes to `runs` + `documents` + Storage (RG-006) instead of
   `companies/<slug>/<slug>/`. The `review` dict it builds maps field-for-field onto the `runs`
   columns — keep the same keys.
4. **Compilation.** `compile_pdfs` calls the LaTeX service (RG-035), not a local binary.
5. **Clients.** Injected per run with the user's BYOK credentials (RG-031), never constructed
   from environment defaults inside the graph.

### What must not change
`route_after_review` in full: the total-call cap, the revision-call cap, the max-revisions cap,
the empty-`failing_documents` exit, **and the <50% fix-resolution-rate bail-out**. The cover
letter still generates exactly once, after the loop. `failing_documents` still considers both
`resume_score` and `ats_total_score`. `ats_check_resume` still swallows its own errors into
`ats_error`. `build_persist_warnings` still runs. `strip_code_fence` still runs on every LLM
output. `_ensure_llm_budget` still guards every provider call.

Note a latent v1 bug to fix in passing: `build_persist_warnings` references
`COVER_LETTER_PASS_SCORE`, which is not imported in `graph.py`. Import it from `budgets.py`.

### Reuse from v1
`graph.py`, `state.py`, `jd_loader.py` — near-verbatim. `tests/test_graph_helpers.py`,
`test_graph_integration.py`, `test_jd_loader.py` — the regression net for this whole ticket.

### Tests
- All ported v1 tests pass.
- New: routing table test over `route_after_review` — one case per exit condition, including the
  fix-resolution bail-out.
- New: two concurrent runs for different users produce independent final states.
- New: a run resumed from its checkpoint after a simulated process restart completes correctly.

### Definition of done
Ported tests green, routing table complete, concurrency test green.

### Out of scope
HTTP routes (RG-032), ATS internals (RG-033), compilation (RG-035).

Title: RG-031 — Provider abstraction and per-user model budgets
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 hard-splits work between a Claude review client and an OpenAI generation client
with env-var keys and global call caps. v2 needs the same split, but per user, with the user's
keys and their own ceilings.

**User story.** As a user I choose which model handles generation, review, and revision, and I
set how many revision cycles a run may spend.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Three model roles are configurable: generation, review, revision.
- A run stops at my configured budget, and tells me it stopped rather than failing silently.
- A hard server-side ceiling above my setting protects me from a runaway configuration.
- A provider outage produces a retryable, named error — not a stack trace.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/llm/base.py         LLMClient protocol: complete(system, user, max_tokens)
apps/api/resume_api/llm/anthropic.py    ← v1 claude_client.py
apps/api/resume_api/llm/openai.py       ← v1 openai_client.py
apps/api/resume_api/llm/catalog.py      ← v1 catalog.py, extended with pricing
apps/api/resume_api/llm/factory.py      ← v1 factory.py, now user-scoped
apps/api/resume_api/llm/pricing.py
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/budgets.py
```

### Budget contract
Defaults are v1's numbers, now per-user editable with a server ceiling:

| Setting | v1 | Default | User max | Server ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| max_revisions | 1 | 1 | 5 | 5 |
| resume_pass_score | 8.0 | 8.0 | 9.5 | — |
| ats_pass_threshold | 80 | 80 | 95 | — |
| max_total_llm_calls | 16 | 16 | 24 | 30 |
| max_openai_calls | 4 | 4 | 8 | 10 |
| max_claude_calls | 8 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
| max_revision_calls | 5 | 5 | 8 | 10 |

### Steps
1. Keep `parse_strict_json_object` from v1's `claude_client.py` — the review and targeting nodes
   depend on strict JSON parsing, and it already handles fenced output.
2. `factory.for_run(user_id, profile)` resolves the three role clients from the profile's model
   choices plus the user's decrypted keys, raising `missing_api_key` before the graph starts.
3. Retries: 3 attempts, exponential backoff with jitter, on 429 and 5xx only. Never retry a 400 —
   that is a prompt bug and retrying burns the user's money.
4. `_ensure_llm_budget` reads the per-run budget object rather than module constants. Exceeding a
   budget raises `BudgetExceeded`, which the graph turns into a persisted warning, exactly as v1
   does — a budget stop still produces usable output.
5. Every call goes through `telemetry.record_llm_call` (RG-007).

### Reuse from v1
`llm/factory.py`, `catalog.py`, `claude_client.py`, `openai_client.py` — ported.
`tests/test_model_catalog.py` — ported. `cli_proxy/` — **dropped**, do not port.

### Tests
- Ported catalog test passes.
- A fake client that always 429s retries three times, then raises `upstream_failed`.
- A 400 is not retried.
- A user budget above the server ceiling is clamped to the ceiling, not honoured.

### Definition of done
Tests green; budgets visible in the run record.

### Out of scope
Settings UI (RG-047).

Title: RG-032 — Run orchestration and live progress
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 streams graph nodes straight into the Streamlit process. If the tab closes, the
run is gone. A generation takes minutes and makes real, paid LLM calls — losing one is expensive.

**User story.** As a user I start a generation, watch each stage complete, navigate away, close
the tab, come back, and still see the run's progress and its result.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Starting a run returns immediately with a run id.
- Progress is visible within a second of each stage completing.
- Refreshing the page mid-run resumes the live view with no lost events.
- A failed run shows which stage failed and why, in one sentence.
- A run can be cancelled, and cancelling stops further LLM spend.

## Technical plan

Decision D4: FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` for v2.0, with run state entirely in Postgres so the swap
to a real queue is an enqueue-call change.

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/routers/runs.py
apps/api/resume_api/services/run_service.py     create, execute, cancel
apps/api/resume_api/services/run_events.py      append + SSE tail
apps/web/src/hooks/useRunStream.ts
```

### Routes
```
POST   /v1/applications/{id}/runs      { template_id?, compile_pdf } → { run_id } (202)
GET    /v1/runs/{id}                   full run record
GET    /v1/runs/{id}/events            SSE: replay all, then tail
POST   /v1/runs/{id}/cancel
```

### Event contract
One event per completed graph node, plus lifecycle events:
```json
{ "seq": 4, "node": "review_documents", "status": "completed",
  "label": "Reviewed against the rubric",
  "payload": { "resume_score": 8.4, "revision_count": 0 },
  "at": "2026-07-31T14:02:11Z" }
```
`label` is arey-voice display copy computed server-side, so the client never maps node names to
prose. `payload` carries only scalars — never document bodies.

### Steps
1. `POST /runs` validates: JD present and ≥ 300 chars (v1's `MIN_JD_TEXT_LENGTH`), keys resolvable
   (RG-023), a template selected or recommendable. It writes `runs(status='queued')` and returns
   before any LLM call. All preflight failures are 400s with named codes.
2. Execution wraps v1's `stream_graph` generator: for each `(node_name, node_state)` yielded,
   append a `run_events` row in the same transaction as the `runs` partial update. Ordering comes
   from a per-run `seq` sequence, so replay is exact.
3. SSE handler: `?after_seq=N` replays everything after N from the table, then tails via Postgres
   `LISTEN/NOTIFY`. Heartbeat comment every 15 s so proxies do not drop the connection.
4. `useRunStream` reconnects with the last seen `seq`, so a refresh or a dropped connection loses
   nothing. On `succeeded` it invalidates the run query and stops.
5. Cancellation sets `runs.status='cancelled'`; the executor checks the flag between nodes and
   stops. Mid-node LLM calls are allowed to finish — killing them wastes the spend already made.
6. Terminal states always write `finished_at`, and `error` on failure. A crashed process leaves a
   run `running`; a startup sweep marks runs older than 30 minutes as `failed` with a stale-run
   message.

### Reuse from v1
`graph.stream_graph` — the streaming generator already yields exactly the right granularity.
v1's `app.py run_generation` shows which node names map to which user-facing stage labels.

### Tests
- Start → all events appear in order → run reaches `succeeded`.
- Disconnect after seq 3, reconnect with `after_seq=3`, receive 4..n with no gap and no duplicate.
- Cancel mid-run: status is `cancelled`, and no further `run_events` are appended.
- Preflight: a 200-char JD is rejected with `jd_too_short` and no run row is created.

### Definition of done
Four tests green; a refresh mid-run visibly resumes.

### Out of scope
The generation screen UI (RG-042).

Title: RG-033 — ATS checker as a service module
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The ATS scorer is a separate local package (`ats-checker/`) that v1 imports
opportunistically and tolerates the absence of. It is one of the product's two headline numbers,
so it needs to be a first-class, always-present dependency — and reachable on its own, so an
imported resume can be scored without generating anything.

**User story.** As a user I see an ATS score with its keyword, structural, and semantic
components, what matched, what is missing, and the highest-value actions — for a generated resume
or one I imported.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The same resume and JD always produce the same score. No LLM in this path.
- Missing keywords are split into required and preferred.
- Unmet hard requirements are listed explicitly.
- A score can be requested for any resume text, outside a generation run.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/ats/                  vendored from ats-checker/ats_checker/
  __init__.py action_verbs.py config.py hard_requirements.py jd_cleaner.py
  keyword_extractor.py resume_parser.py scorer.py section_parser.py synonyms.py
apps/api/resume_api/services/ats_service.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/ats.py
apps/api/tests/ats/                       ← ats-checker/tests/
```

### Routes
```
POST /v1/ats/check    { resume_text | document_id, jd_text } → AtsResult
```

### Contract — keep v1's key names exactly
```
ats_total_score, ats_grade, ats_keyword_score, ats_structural_score, ats_semantic_score,
ats_matched[], ats_missing_required[], ats_missing_preferred[], ats_top_actions[],
ats_hard_requirements[{description, met}], ats_all_hard_met, ats_error
```
These are the keys `graph.persist_outputs` writes and the result view reads. Renaming them
breaks the port for no gain.

### Steps
1. Vendor the package into `apps/api/resume_api/ats/` as a real dependency (it is the maintainer's
   own code; a git submodule would add friction for no benefit). Record the source commit in a
   header comment. Bring its tests.
2. `ats_service.check(resume_tex, jd_text)` wraps it, strips LaTeX to plain text before scoring
   (the scorer expects prose, not markup), and returns the dict above. It **never raises** — any
   failure returns `{"ats_error": "..."}`, preserving v1's behaviour where a bad ATS check does
   not kill a run.
3. `ATS_PASS_THRESHOLD = 80` ("Excellent") stays the pass bar, now per-user overridable (RG-031).
4. The standalone route is what makes the import flow (RG-044) work.

### Reuse from v1
The entire `ats-checker` package, verbatim. `resume_agent/ats_client.py` shows the wrapping
contract. `graph.ats_check_resume` shows the error-tolerance requirement.

### Tests
- Ported `ats-checker` tests pass unchanged.
- Determinism: the same input scored twice is byte-identical.
- A malformed JD returns `ats_error` and does not raise.
- LaTeX stripping: a `.tex` resume and its plain-text equivalent score within 2 points.

### Definition of done
Ported tests green plus the four above.

### Out of scope
The ATS UI and evidence gate (RG-036, RG-043).

Title: RG-034 — Review rubric and scoring service
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The human-reviewer score is the product's other headline number. In v1 it is a
weighted rubric computed in `scoring.py` from category scores the reviewer model returns.

**User story.** As a user I see not just an overall score but the eight weighted categories
behind it, so I know what to fix.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The overall score is reproducible from the category scores shown.
- A reviewer response missing a category degrades gracefully — that category scores zero and is
  reported as missing, rather than the run failing.
- The category weights are visible in the UI.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/pipeline/scoring.py     ← v1 scoring.py, verbatim
apps/api/tests/test_scoring.py              ← v1, verbatim
packages/contracts/src/rubric.ts            weights mirrored for display
```

### The rubric — do not change these weights
Resume: jd_skills_keyword_match .20 · role_domain_relevance .15 ·
achievement_evidence_strength .15 · credibility_source_truth_compliance .15 ·
single_page_compliance .15 · targeting_brief_compliance .10 ·
ats_latex_formatting_safety .05 · recruiter_impression_seniority_alignment .05

Cover letter: jd_company_alignment .30 · evidence_relevance .25 · motivation_domain_fit .20 ·
clarity_tone .15 · credibility_no_fabrication .10

### Steps
1. Copy `scoring.py` across with no edits. `weighted_score` clamps each category to 0–10, treats
   a missing category as 0, and reports it in `missing_categories` — keep all of that.
2. Mirror the weights into `packages/contracts/src/rubric.ts` for the result view, and add a test
   asserting the TS weights sum to 1.0 and match the Python dict key-for-key. Two copies of a
   constant is acceptable only with a test that keeps them honest.

### Reuse from v1
`resume_agent/scoring.py` and `tests/test_scoring.py` — verbatim, both.

### Tests
- Ported test passes unchanged.
- Python and TS rubrics agree (key set and weights).

### Definition of done
Both green.

### Out of scope
Rendering (RG-043).

Title: RG-035 — LaTeX compilation service
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 shells out to a local LaTeX install. Most machines do not have one, and in a
multi-user product the `.tex` being compiled is untrusted user input.

**User story.** As a user I edit the LaTeX of my resume, press compile, and get a PDF in a few
seconds — or a readable error pointing at the line that broke.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Compilation works with no LaTeX installed on the API host or the user's machine.
- A malicious `.tex` cannot read the filesystem, reach the network, or run a shell.
- Compilation fails fast — no run hangs on a LaTeX error prompt.
- A failure shows the first meaningful error line, not 400 lines of log.

## Technical plan

Decision D2: a Tectonic container as a separate service.

### Files
```
services/latex/Dockerfile              tectonic on a slim base
services/latex/app.py                  POST /compile → application/pdf | 422 + parsed error
services/latex/parse_log.py            TeX log → first meaningful error {line, message}
apps/api/resume_api/services/latex.py  client
apps/api/resume_api/routers/compile.py
```

### Routes
```
POST /v1/documents/{id}/compile    → { document_id (pdf), pages, warnings[] }
POST /v1/compile/preview           { tex } → same, not persisted (LaTeX editor preview)
```

### Hardening (all required)
- `tectonic -X compile --untrusted`, which disables shell-escape and external commands.
- Container runs as a non-root user, read-only root filesystem, scratch on a tmpfs.
- No network egress from the container except the Tectonic package cache, which is **pre-warmed
  into the image** at build time so runtime egress can be blocked entirely.
- 20 s wall-clock timeout, 512 MB memory, 1 CPU. `-halt-on-error` so it never waits for input.
- Input capped at 200 KB, and re-run through the RG-021 macro denylist before compiling.

### Steps
1. Two-pass compile (references and page counts need it); parse the log after the final pass.
2. `parse_log.py` returns the first `! ` line with its `l.NNN` line number and a one-sentence
   summary. Full log goes to the response `details`, never into the user-facing message.
3. On success, store the PDF via `BlobStore` and insert a `documents` row of kind `*_pdf`.
4. `compile_pdfs` in the graph calls this service and preserves v1's behaviour exactly: failures
   populate `compile_errors` and the run still ends `complete_with_compile_errors` — a PDF failure
   never loses the `.tex`.
5. Cache by `sha256(tex)`: identical source returns the stored PDF without recompiling.

### Reuse from v1
`resume_agent/latex_compile.py` for the interface shape (`compile_tex_file(src, out, requested)`
→ `success`/`error`) and `graph.compile_pdfs` for the error-tolerance contract. The subprocess
implementation itself is replaced.

### Tests
- A known-good template compiles to a PDF with the expected page count.
- A `.tex` with a deliberate error returns 422 with the correct line number.
- A `\write18{...}` payload is rejected before reaching Tectonic.
- An infinite `\loop` is killed by the timeout and returns a timeout error, not a hang.
- The hash cache returns the second request without invoking Tectonic (assert via a call counter).

### Definition of done
All five tests green; the container image builds in CI.

### Out of scope
The LaTeX editor UI (RG-043).

Title: RG-036 — Evidence-gated ATS keyword fixes
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The fastest way to raise an ATS score is to paste in missing keywords. That is also
how a resume becomes a lie and a candidate gets caught in an interview. The product's position is
that a keyword may only be added if the user can point at where they actually did it.

**User story.** The ATS panel says I am missing "Kubernetes". To add it, I must attach a company
or project from my source of truth and a specific experience bullet that evidences it. Once I do,
the keyword is added to the resume **and** saved back to my source of truth, so every future
resume knows it.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A missing keyword cannot be accepted without both an owning company/project and a bullet.
- Accepting writes the evidence into the source of truth, not just into this one resume.
- I can write a new bullet inline while accepting, and it is saved to the source of truth too.
- I can dismiss a keyword as not applicable, and it stays dismissed for this application.
- The resume is regenerated or patched with the keyword only after the evidence exists.

## Technical plan

This is the product's most opinionated feature. It has no v1 equivalent — build it carefully.

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/schemas/evidence.py
apps/api/resume_api/services/evidence_service.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/evidence.py
supabase/migrations/0015_keyword_decisions.sql
```

### Schema
`keyword_decisions` — user_id, application_id, run_id, keyword citext,
decision `('accepted','dismissed','deferred')`, sot_company_id null, sot_project_id null,
sot_bullet_id null, created_bullet bool, note, created_at.
Unique `(application_id, lower(keyword))`.

### Routes
```
GET  /v1/runs/{id}/keywords                  missing + matched + prior decisions, merged
POST /v1/runs/{id}/keywords/{kw}/accept      { company_id | project_id, bullet_id | new_bullet }
POST /v1/runs/{id}/keywords/{kw}/dismiss     { note? }
POST /v1/runs/{id}/keywords/apply            regenerate the resume with the accepted set
```

### The gate — server-enforced, not a UI convention
`accept` rejects with `evidence_required` unless:
1. exactly one of `company_id` / `project_id` is present and owned by the caller; **and**
2. either `bullet_id` (owned, and belonging to that company or project) or `new_bullet` with at
   least 40 characters of text is present.

On success, in one transaction:
- if `new_bullet`: insert an `sot_bullets` row under that company/project;
- upsert an `sot_skills` row for the keyword, appending the bullet id to `evidence_bullet_ids`;
- insert the `keyword_decisions` row.

The source-of-truth write is the point of the feature. A keyword accepted here is permanently
part of the user's record and will be available to every future application. This is what makes
the gate a compounding asset rather than a nag.

### `apply`
Runs the revision node once with the accepted keywords and their evidence bullets appended to the
prompt context, then re-runs the ATS check, and writes a new `runs` row linked to the same
application. It never edits the previous run — score history stays intact.

### Tests
- Accept with no bullet → `evidence_required`; nothing is written (assert the transaction rolled back).
- Accept with a bullet belonging to a different company → rejected.
- Accept with `new_bullet` → the bullet exists in the source of truth afterwards and the skill row
  references it.
- Dismiss persists across a page reload and across a re-run of the ATS check.
- `apply` produces a new run whose ATS score is ≥ the previous one for a seeded fixture.

### Definition of done
All five tests green; the gate is impossible to bypass through the API.

### Out of scope
The panel UI (RG-043).

Title: RG-037 — Import an existing resume for scoring
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** Users already have resumes they have sent out. v1 can only score what it generates,
so all that history is invisible to the tracker and gets no feedback.

**User story.** I upload or paste a resume I already sent, attach the job description, and get
the same ATS and review scores as a generated one — and it appears in my pipeline alongside
everything else.

**Acceptance criteria**
- I can import by `.tex`, `.pdf`, or pasted text.
- An imported application is scored on both dimensions and marked clearly as imported.
- Imported applications appear in the pipeline and can be tracked through interview rounds.
- I can convert an imported application into a generated one, reusing its job description.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/services/import_service.py
apps/api/resume_api/routers/imports.py
apps/api/resume_api/parsers/pdf_text.py       pypdf extraction
apps/api/resume_api/parsers/tex_text.py       LaTeX → plain text (shared with RG-033)
```

### Routes
```
POST /v1/applications/import      multipart: file? + { company_name, job_title, jd_text, resume_text? }
                                  → { application_id, run_id }
POST /v1/applications/{id}/convert-to-generated  → { application_id }
```

### Steps
1. Create the `applications` row with `source = 'imported'`, store the original file as a
   `documents` row of kind `imported_resume`.
2. Extract text: `.tex` → `tex_text`; `.pdf` → `pypdf`, and if the extraction yields under 200
   characters, reject with `unreadable_pdf` ("This looks like a scanned PDF. Paste the text
   instead.") rather than scoring garbage. No OCR in v2.0.
3. Create a `runs` row with `status='succeeded'` that skips generation entirely and runs only two
   stages: `ats_check` (RG-033) and `review_documents` (the reviewer prompt against the imported
   text, so the scores are comparable to a generated run).
4. Emit `run_events` for both stages so the same UI (RG-042) renders the import progress.
5. `convert-to-generated` creates a **new** application seeded with the same company, title, and
   JD, linked back via `derived_from`. The import is never mutated.

### Reuse from v1
The reviewer prompt and `scoring.attach_scores` are used unchanged, which is what makes an
imported score directly comparable to a generated one.

### Tests
- `.tex`, `.pdf`, and pasted-text imports each produce a run with both scores.
- A scanned (image-only) PDF returns `unreadable_pdf` and creates no application.
- An imported application appears in the pipeline list with the imported marker.
- Convert creates a new application and leaves the original untouched.

### Definition of done
All four tests green.

### Out of scope
The import UI (RG-044).

Title: RG-040 — Pipeline screen (application tracker)
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1's "Applied Jobs" tab lists folders on disk with a status dropdown. It cannot
answer the question a job search actually asks: what needs my attention today.

**User story.** I open the app and immediately see every application, where each one stands, and
what I owe it next.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every application shows company, role, both scores, status, and last activity.
- I can filter by status and search by company or role.
- Generated and imported applications are visually distinguishable at a glance.
- I can advance status and record an interview round without leaving the list.
- With no applications, the empty state offers exactly two actions: generate, or import.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/pipeline/page.tsx           server component, initial fetch
apps/web/src/components/pipeline/ApplicationTable.tsx
apps/web/src/components/pipeline/StatusCell.tsx    inline status change
apps/web/src/components/pipeline/ScorePair.tsx     ATS + review, mono numerals
apps/web/src/components/pipeline/PipelineFilters.tsx
apps/web/src/components/pipeline/RoundTracker.tsx  popover: round count, current round, next action
apps/api/resume_api/routers/applications.py        list, patch status
```

### Presentation
Columns: **Company / role** (two-line cell, role in `--text-secondary`) · **Source** (a Badge:
"Generated" / "Imported") · **ATS** · **Review** · **Status** · **Next action** · **Updated**.

Per the arey guide: all numbers and timestamps in `--font-mono`. Relative time in the cell
("3 d ago"), absolute in the tooltip. Status is a colour dot plus a label — never a coloured row
background, never a left-border stripe. Scores show as `82` and `8.4` with the threshold implied
by the dot colour, not by a progress bar in every row.

Below 940px the table becomes a stacked card list; the same data, no horizontal scroll.

### Steps
