1. Server-render the first page; TanStack Query takes over for filtering and mutation.
2. Filters are URL state (`?status=&q=`), so a filtered view is linkable and survives a refresh.
3. Status change is an optimistic `PATCH /v1/applications/{id}`, reverting with a toast on failure.
4. `RoundTracker` edits `round_count`, `current_round`, and `next_action` in a popover — v1's
   `application_status.json` fields, now first-class.
5. Cursor pagination at 50 rows with an infinite-scroll sentinel.
6. Empty state: one line ("No applications yet.") and two buttons. No illustration.

### Reuse from v1
`app.py render_application_browser` / `_application_row` for the field set and the status
vocabulary; `storage.default_application_status()` for the exact fields to expose.

### Tests
- Playwright: filter by status narrows the list and updates the URL.
- Optimistic status change reverts and toasts when the API 500s.
- The imported marker renders for an imported application.
- Empty state renders both actions for a new user.

### Definition of done
Four tests green at 360px and 1440px.

### Out of scope
Bulk actions, CSV export.

Title: RG-041 — New application: input and launch
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1's generate tab asks for company, title, and a JD, then runs. It gives no
confidence about what is about to happen or what it will cost.

**User story.** I paste a job description, confirm the template the system suggests, and start —
knowing which models will run and roughly what it will cost before I commit.

**Acceptance criteria**
- I can supply the JD by paste or URL, and see it was fetched successfully before starting.
- A template is recommended with a stated reason, and I can override it.
- I see which three models will run and an estimated cost before pressing start.
- A JD under 300 characters blocks the start with a clear reason.
- Pressing start navigates straight to the live run view.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/new/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/generate/JdInput.tsx           tabs: paste | URL
apps/web/src/components/generate/TemplatePicker.tsx    recommendation + override
apps/web/src/components/generate/RunPreflight.tsx      models, budget, estimated cost
```

### Steps
1. Three fields — company, job title, JD — then a preflight card. No wizard, no multi-step form;
   it is four inputs and a button.
2. JD by URL calls `POST /v1/jd/fetch` (thin wrapper on v1's `jd_loader.fetch_jd_from_url`),
   showing the fetched character count and the first lines so the user can confirm it worked.
   v1's `MIN_JD_TEXT_LENGTH` guard is surfaced inline, not as a post-submit error.
3. On JD blur, call `POST /v1/templates/recommend` and show the recommendation with its reason
   as helper text. Overriding it is a Select; the reason stays visible.
4. `RunPreflight` lists the three model roles from the profile, the revision ceiling, and an
   estimated cost from `llm/pricing.py`. Estimated, and labelled as such — never presented as exact.
5. Start posts to `POST /v1/applications` then `POST /v1/applications/{id}/runs` and routes to
   `/applications/{id}/runs/{runId}`.
6. Autosave the draft to `localStorage` per user, so a long JD paste survives an accidental reload.

### Reuse from v1
`app.py render_generation_tab` for the field set; `jd_loader.py` for URL fetch and the length
guard; `resume_selection.py` for the recommendation and its reason string.

### Tests
- A 200-char JD disables start and explains why.
- URL fetch failure shows the loader's error message inline, and start stays disabled.
- The recommendation appears after entering a JD and can be overridden.
- Start creates an application and lands on the run route.

### Definition of done
Four tests green.

### Out of scope
The live run view (RG-042).

Title: RG-042 — Live run view
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** A generation takes minutes and makes up to sixteen paid LLM calls. Silence during
that time reads as a hang, and v1 loses the run if the tab closes.

**User story.** I watch each stage complete with a plain-language label, I can leave and come
back, and when it finishes I land on the result.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Each stage appears as it completes, with elapsed time.
- Revision cycles are shown as cycles, not as a confusing repeat of the same stage.
- Refreshing mid-run resumes the view with no lost or duplicated stages.
- On failure I see which stage failed and one sentence about why, with a retry.
- I can cancel.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/[id]/runs/[runId]/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/run/RunTimeline.tsx
apps/web/src/components/run/RunStage.tsx
apps/web/src/hooks/useRunStream.ts        (from RG-032)
```

### Stage labels — server-supplied (RG-032), listed here for design reference
`resolve_jd_input` "Read the job description" · `load_inputs` "Loaded your source of truth" ·
`create_targeting_brief` "Built the targeting brief" · `generate_resume` "Wrote the resume" ·
`review_documents` "Reviewed against the rubric" · `ats_check_resume` "Scored for ATS" ·
`revise_documents` "Revised the resume" · `generate_cover_letter` "Wrote the cover letter" ·
`persist_outputs` "Saved" · `compile_pdfs` "Compiled the PDF"

### Presentation
A vertical timeline. Completed stages show a filled Phosphor check and a mono elapsed time
(`4.2 s`). The active stage shows a Spinner in place of the glyph. Pending stages are
`--text-tertiary`. Repeat passes group under a "Revision 1" subheading rather than appending a
duplicate row — this is where v1's stream is confusing.

Review and ATS stages surface their score in the row as it lands, so the user sees the number
climb across revisions. That is the most reassuring thing the screen can do.

Motion is opacity + 4px rise at 220ms per stage. Nothing bounces. Reduced motion zeroes it.

### Steps
1. Subscribe via `useRunStream(runId, afterSeq)`; seed `afterSeq` from the server-rendered events
   already in the page so a refresh never replays what is already shown.
2. On `succeeded`, redirect to the result view after a 600ms beat so the last stage is visible.
3. On `failed`, render the failing stage in the error state with `errors.ts` copy and a "Start
   again" button that reuses the same inputs.
4. Cancel is a quiet Button with a confirm Dialog stating that work already spent is not refunded.

### Reuse from v1
`app.py run_generation`'s node-to-label mapping and its ordering.

### Tests
- Mocked SSE: stages render in order with elapsed times.
- Mid-run refresh shows all prior stages exactly once.
- A failure event renders the error state and the retry.
- Two revision cycles group under separate subheadings.

### Definition of done
Four tests green.

### Out of scope
The result view (RG-043).

Title: RG-043 — Result view: scores, ATS panel, and LaTeX editor
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** This is the screen the whole product exists to show. v1 splits it across tabs and
buries the scores below the LaTeX.

**User story.** I see how the resume scored on both dimensions, exactly what is missing, what I
can honestly do about it, and I can edit the LaTeX and recompile without leaving the page.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Both scores are the first thing on the page, with their category and component breakdowns one
  interaction away.
- Missing ATS keywords are actionable through the evidence gate — never a one-click "add".
- The LaTeX is visible, editable, and recompilable, with the PDF beside it.
- Warnings from the run are shown, not hidden.
- I can download the `.tex` and the `.pdf` for both the resume and the cover letter.

## Technical plan

**Size warning.** This ticket is XL. If it must be split, cut along the three panels below —
each is independently shippable behind the same route.

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/[id]/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/result/ScoreHero.tsx          the two headline numbers
apps/web/src/components/result/ReviewPanel.tsx        8 rubric categories, weights, must-fix list
apps/web/src/components/result/AtsPanel.tsx           components, matched, missing, hard reqs
apps/web/src/components/result/KeywordGate.tsx        the evidence dialog (RG-036)
apps/web/src/components/result/TexEditor.tsx          CodeMirror 6, LaTeX mode
apps/web/src/components/result/PdfPreview.tsx         pdf.js, page nav
apps/web/src/components/result/WarningsList.tsx
apps/web/src/components/result/DownloadMenu.tsx
```

### Layout
`ScoreHero` full width at the top: two large mono numerals — ATS `82 / 100` with its grade, and
review `8.4 / 10` — each with a one-line verdict and a threshold marker. No dials, no gauges, no
gradients; the number *is* the graphic. Below, a three-tab `Tabs`: **Review**, **ATS**,
**Documents**. Above 1200px, Documents renders as a two-pane split (editor left, PDF right);
below that it is a `SegmentedControl` between the two.

### `AtsPanel` and the gate
Missing keywords list as Tags in two groups, required and preferred. Clicking one opens
`KeywordGate`, a Dialog that requires:
1. a company or project, picked from the user's source of truth (searchable Select);
2. a bullet — either an existing one under that company/project, or a new one typed inline
   (minimum 40 characters, with the helper text "Describe what you actually did with it").

The primary Button stays disabled until both are satisfied. There is no bypass, no "add anyway".
On success the Tag moves from missing to matched, and a quiet line confirms it was saved to the
source of truth — that confirmation is important; it tells the user the work compounds.

"Not applicable" dismisses the keyword with an optional note.

An "Apply accepted keywords" Button appears once at least one is accepted; it calls
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/keywords/apply` and routes to the new run's live view.

### `TexEditor`
CodeMirror 6, `--font-mono`, LaTeX syntax highlighting, line numbers. Debounced local autosave;
explicit "Save and compile" for the server round-trip. Compile errors render inline at the
reported line (RG-035) and as a summary above the editor. Never block editing while compiling.

### `ReviewPanel`
The eight categories as rows: name, weight (mono), score out of 10, and the reviewer's comment.
The must-fix list above them, as the reviewer returned it. Both come straight from
`runs.resume_review`.

### Reuse from v1
`app.py render_result`, `_render_ats_tab`, `render_tex_editor` for the information architecture —
v1 already decided what to show; this ticket decides how. `runs.ats` and `runs.resume_review`
carry v1's exact key names, so the panels read them directly.

### Tests
- `ScoreHero` renders both scores with mono numerals and the correct grade band.
- The gate's primary button is disabled without evidence and enabled with it.
- Accepting a keyword moves the tag and shows the source-of-truth confirmation.
- Editing the LaTeX and compiling updates the PDF preview.
- A compile error renders at the correct line.
- Run warnings appear on the page.
- `jest-axe`: the dialog traps focus and returns it on close.

### Definition of done
Seven tests green; the split layout works at 1200px and collapses cleanly below.

### Out of scope
Version diffing between runs.

Title: RG-044 — Import flow UI
Description:
## Product requirement

**User story.** I have already applied to twelve jobs with a resume I wrote myself. I want those
in the tracker, scored, so I know which ones were weak and what to fix next time.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Import by drag-and-drop file, file picker, or paste.
- I supply the company, role, and job description alongside the resume.
- I see the same two scores as a generated application.
- A scanned PDF tells me plainly to paste the text instead.
- Importing is reachable from the pipeline empty state and from the sidebar.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/applications/import/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/import/ResumeDropzone.tsx     .tex, .pdf, ≤5 MB
apps/web/src/components/import/ImportForm.tsx
```

### Steps
1. Dropzone accepts `.tex` and `.pdf`; a third tab accepts pasted text. On file selection show
   the filename, size (mono), and the extracted character count as a confidence signal.
2. Same company / role / JD fields as RG-041, sharing the components — not a second copy.
3. Submit posts multipart to `POST /v1/applications/import` and routes to the run view, which
   shows only the two scoring stages (RG-042 handles this without change).
4. `unreadable_pdf` renders inline on the dropzone with the paste tab pre-selected — recover the
   user in place rather than sending them back to the start.
5. On the result view, an imported application shows an "Imported" Badge next to the title and a
   "Generate a tailored version" Button calling `convert-to-generated`.

### Tests
- Drag-and-drop a `.tex` → import succeeds and lands on the run view.
- An oversized file is rejected client-side with a clear message.
- `unreadable_pdf` switches to the paste tab with the error shown.
- The imported badge and the convert action render on the result view.

### Definition of done
Four tests green.

### Out of scope
Bulk import.

Title: RG-045 — Source of truth and prompts screen
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** These are the two things that determine output quality, and in v1 both are files on
disk that a user cannot reach.

**User story.** I curate my career record and, separately, tune the instructions the system uses
at each stage — and I can always get back to the defaults.

**Acceptance criteria**
- I can manage companies, projects, bullets, and skills with inline editing and drag reorder.
- I can see exactly the text that gets injected into prompts.
- I can edit all six prompts, see version history, restore a version, and reset to default.
- A prompt missing a required variable cannot be saved, and the error names the variable.
- Nothing is lost on an accidental navigation.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/source-of-truth/page.tsx        Tabs: Career record | Prompts
apps/web/src/components/sot/CompanyList.tsx            accordion, dnd-kit reorder
apps/web/src/components/sot/BulletEditor.tsx           inline textarea, autosave
apps/web/src/components/sot/SkillGrid.tsx              category groups, evidence links
apps/web/src/components/sot/RenderedPreview.tsx        read-only, mono, the injected text
apps/web/src/components/prompts/PromptEditor.tsx       CodeMirror, variable chips
apps/web/src/components/prompts/VersionHistory.tsx
```

### Steps
1. **Career record tab.** Companies as an accordion; each holds projects, each holds bullets.
   `dnd-kit` for reorder, committing to `POST /source-of-truth/reorder` on drop. Bullet edits
   autosave on blur with a quiet "Saved" — no save button, no dialog.
2. A skill row shows the bullets that evidence it as small links. A skill with no evidence shows
   a quiet warning glyph — this is the same standard the ATS gate enforces, applied to the record
   itself, so the two features feel like one idea.
3. `RenderedPreview` is a collapsed panel showing `GET /source-of-truth/rendered` verbatim in
   `--font-mono`. Making the prompt input visible is what lets a user debug bad output themselves.
4. **Prompts tab.** Six stages down the left as a `SidebarNav`; the editor on the right. Above the
   editor, the required variables render as `Kbd`-style chips — clicking one inserts it at the
   cursor. A chip is muted when that variable is absent from the body, so a missing one is visible
   before saving, not only on the validation error.
5. A customised prompt shows a "Modified" Badge in the stage list and a "Reset to default" action.
   `VersionHistory` is a popover listing versions with timestamps (mono) and a restore action.
6. `beforeunload` guard on unsaved prompt edits. The career record does not need one — it autosaves.

### Reuse from v1
`base/source_of_truth.txt` for the record's shape and the rendered format;
`resume_agent/prompts/*.md` as the default bodies shown when a user resets.

### Tests
- Reordering bullets persists across a reload.
- The rendered preview matches `GET /rendered` exactly.
- Saving a prompt without `{{JD_TEXT}}` shows the named error and does not save.
- Restoring a version replaces the editor body.
- Reset restores the system default and clears the "Modified" badge.

### Definition of done
Five tests green.

### Out of scope
Importing a career record from LinkedIn or a PDF.

Title: RG-046 — Templates screen
Description:
## Product requirement

**User story.** I keep a small library of LaTeX resume templates, see what each one looks like,
and add my own by uploading, pasting, or copying an existing one.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every template shows a rendered preview, not just a filename.
- I can add one three ways, and validation problems are explained before I save.
- I can duplicate any template, including the system ones, and edit my copy.
- I cannot delete a system template, and deleting one that is in use explains why.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/templates/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/templates/TemplateGrid.tsx
apps/web/src/components/templates/TemplateCard.tsx      preview thumbnail + actions
apps/web/src/components/templates/AddTemplateDialog.tsx tabs: upload | paste | duplicate
apps/web/src/components/templates/TemplatePreview.tsx   first-page render
```

### Steps
1. Grid of Cards. Each: preview thumbnail, name, kind Badge ("Single page" / "Multi page"), a
   "System" Badge where applicable, and a menu with duplicate, edit, delete.
2. Previews are generated once per template by compiling it with placeholder content (RG-035) and
   caching the first page as a PNG in Storage. Compile-on-view would be far too slow for a grid.
3. `AddTemplateDialog`: upload validates client-side for `.tex` and 200 KB, then server-side
   (RG-021); paste uses CodeMirror; duplicate is a Select over the library plus a name field.
4. Validation errors list every problem at once, in arey voice: "Line 40 uses \\write18. Remove it
   and save again."
5. Deleting a template in use surfaces the 409 as "Used by 3 applications. Duplicate it instead."

### Reuse from v1
`single_page/*.tex` and `multi_page/*.tex` are the seeded library; `config.py TEMPLATE_FILES`
gives the naming.

### Tests
- The grid shows ten seeded templates with previews.
- Uploading an invalid `.tex` lists every validation problem.
- Duplicating a system template creates an editable user copy.
- Deleting an in-use template shows the conflict message.

### Definition of done
Four tests green.

### Out of scope
A visual template designer.

Title: RG-047 — Settings screen
Description:
## Product requirement

**User story.** In one place I manage my account, my API keys, the models each stage uses, my
budget ceilings, and my theme.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Adding a key shows only the last four characters afterwards, forever.
- I can test a key before saving it.
- Model choices and budgets are explained in terms of cost and quality, not jargon.
- Theme changes apply immediately and persist across devices.
- Deleting my account is possible, explains what is deleted, and requires typing my email.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx              sections via SidebarNav
apps/web/src/components/settings/AccountSection.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/KeysSection.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/ModelsSection.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/BudgetSection.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/AppearanceSection.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/DangerZone.tsx
```

### Steps
1. Sections: Account, API keys, Models, Budget, Appearance, Danger zone.
2. **Keys.** A row per provider: label, `••••` + last four in mono, created and last-used dates.
   Add opens a Dialog with a masked Input and a "Test key" Button that must pass before Save
   enables. The secret never re-renders after submission.
3. **Models.** Three Selects — generation, review, revision — each showing the model name and its
   per-million-token price in mono. A one-line note explains v1's split: a strong model reviews,
   a cheaper one revises.
4. **Budget.** Sliders for max revisions (1–5) and the call caps, each with the default marked and
   the server ceiling shown. An estimated worst-case cost per run updates live beneath them — this
   is the control that makes BYOK feel safe.
5. **Appearance.** Light / dark / system as a `SegmentedControl`, applying instantly (RG-012).
6. **Danger zone.** Delete account requires typing the email, per the arey guide's rule that
   permanent deletion is confirmed by typing the name. It states exactly what is removed:
   applications, runs, documents, templates, prompts, keys.

### Reuse from v1
`app.py render_sidebar` for the settings that exist; `llm/catalog.py` for the model list;
`config.py` MAX_* values as the defaults shown.

### Tests
- Save is disabled until the key test passes.
- No API response in the network log contains the submitted secret.
- Changing the theme updates `data-theme` immediately and persists after reload.
- Account deletion requires the exact email and is otherwise disabled.

### Definition of done
Four tests green.

### Out of scope
Billing, notification preferences.

Title: RG-048 — Landing page and access screens
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** The product is invite-only, so most visitors cannot sign in. They still need to
understand what it is and be able to ask for access.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A visitor understands in one screen what the product does and why the evidence gate matters.
- Signing in is one click.
- An uninvited visitor lands on register-interest, not on an error.
- The page is fast: no layout shift, no render-blocking third-party script.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/web/src/app/page.tsx                        single column, full width
apps/web/src/components/landing/Hero.tsx
apps/web/src/components/landing/ProductShot.tsx  static screenshot, cool-neutral, hairline + radius
apps/web/src/components/landing/ValueProps.tsx   three, no icon-in-tinted-square grid
apps/web/src/components/landing/HowItWorks.tsx   four numbered steps
apps/web/src/app/(auth)/no-access/page.tsx       register interest
```

### Copy direction (arey voice — declarative, no selling)
Hero: what it does, in one sentence, plus the honest constraint. Something in the register of
"Tailor a resume to a job description, then score it the way an ATS and a human reviewer would."
Sub-line states the position that makes the product different: it will not add a keyword you
cannot evidence.

Three value props, one line each: tailored generation from a single source of truth; scoring on
both dimensions; an evidence gate that keeps the resume true. No exclamation marks. No emoji.

How it works: paste the job description → the system drafts and reviews → you resolve missing
keywords with evidence → export the PDF.

### Steps
1. Single column, `--content-max`, generous 80px section rhythm. Static — no scroll animation,
   no parallax.
2. `ProductShot` is a real screenshot of the result view, desaturated toward the greyscale
   palette, inset with `--radius-card` and a hairline. Reserve its aspect ratio in CSS so there is
   no layout shift. Use `next/image` with a blur placeholder.
3. One primary action, "Sign in with Google", repeated at the top and bottom. Nothing else competes.
4. `/no-access`: one paragraph explaining invite-only, a short form (email, one line about their
   situation) posting to `POST /public/interest`, and a confirmation that does not promise a date.
5. Lighthouse: performance and accessibility both ≥ 95.

### Tests
- Playwright: the sign-in button starts the OAuth flow.
- Register-interest submits and shows the confirmation state.
- Lighthouse CI thresholds enforced in the pipeline.
- No CLS from the product shot (assert the reserved aspect ratio).

### Definition of done
Four checks green.

### Out of scope
Marketing site, blog, pricing.

Title: RG-050 — Run cost accounting
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** BYOK means the user pays directly, so the product owes them an honest number. v1
counts calls but not tokens or money.

**User story.** I see what each run cost me and what I have spent this month.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every run shows a cost broken down by stage.
- A monthly total is visible in settings.
- The estimate shown before a run and the actual after it are within a stated tolerance.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/llm/pricing.py          per-model input/output prices, dated
apps/api/resume_api/routers/usage.py        GET /v1/usage?from=&to=
apps/web/src/components/result/RunCost.tsx
apps/web/src/components/settings/UsageSection.tsx
```

### Steps
1. `pricing.py` is a plain table with an `as_of` date per entry and a test asserting every model
   in `catalog.py` has a price. A missing price is a hard failure, not a silent zero.
2. `record_llm_call` (RG-007) already captures usage per call; roll it into `runs.cost_usd` and
   keep the per-node breakdown in `runs.token_usage`.
3. `RunCost` renders in the result view: total in mono, expandable to per-stage rows.
4. `UsageSection` shows a monthly total and a simple per-day bar list — no charting library for
   this; a list of rows with proportional widths is enough and stays on-brand.

### Tests
- Every catalogued model has a price.
- A three-call run totals correctly across two providers.
- The pre-run estimate is within 25% of actual for a seeded fixture run.

### Definition of done
Three tests green.

### Out of scope
Budgets that hard-stop on spend, invoicing.

Title: RG-051 — Admin portal: invites and users
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** Access is gated by an `allowed_emails` table seeded with SQL. That is fine for the
first cohort and untenable after it.

**User story.** As the operator I add and revoke invited emails and see who has signed in, from
a UI rather than the Supabase console.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Only an admin can reach the portal; everyone else gets a 404, not a 403.
- I can add emails singly or as a pasted list, and revoke access.
- Revoking access signs the user out and blocks the next sign-in, but does not delete their data.
- I can see registered-interest submissions and invite from that list in one action.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
supabase/migrations/0016_admin_flag.sql       profiles.is_admin bool default false
apps/api/resume_api/routers/admin.py          require_admin dependency
apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/page.tsx
apps/web/src/components/admin/{InviteList,InterestList}.tsx
```

### Routes
```
GET    /v1/admin/invites          list with redeemed status
POST   /v1/admin/invites          { emails[] } — accepts a pasted, newline-separated list
DELETE /v1/admin/invites/{email}  revoke
GET    /v1/admin/interest         register-interest submissions
GET    /v1/admin/users            email, signed-up, last active, run count
```

### Steps
1. `require_admin` checks `profiles.is_admin`; the first admin is set by SQL. A non-admin hitting
   any `/v1/admin/*` route gets 404 — do not confirm the surface exists.
2. The web route is hidden from the nav entirely for non-admins, and the page itself returns
   `notFound()`.
3. Bulk add parses a pasted list, normalises and deduplicates emails, and reports which were
   already present rather than erroring.
4. Revoke deletes the `allowed_emails` row and invalidates the user's sessions. Data is retained;
   the sign-in gate does the work.

### Tests
- A non-admin gets 404 on every admin route.
- Bulk add of 20 emails with 3 duplicates reports 17 added, 3 skipped.
- Revoke blocks the next sign-in and leaves the user's applications intact.

### Definition of done
Three tests green.

### Out of scope
Impersonation, per-user quotas.

Title: RG-052 — Move run execution to a queue (conditional)
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** `BackgroundTasks` ties a run's execution to the lifetime of one API process. A
deploy mid-run, or more than a handful of concurrent runs, becomes a real problem.

**Trigger — do not start this ticket until one of these is true:**
- more than five concurrent runs are observed, or
- a deploy has interrupted a run in production, or
- p95 run latency degrades measurably under load.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A deploy during a run does not lose it.
- Runs execute at a bounded concurrency with a queue behind them.
- Nothing about the client's SSE contract changes.

## Technical plan

RG-032 was built to make this a swap, not a redesign: run state already lives in `runs` and
`run_events`, and the executor is a pure function of a run id.

### Files
```
apps/api/resume_api/queue/__init__.py       arq settings + worker entrypoint
apps/api/resume_api/services/run_service.py change: enqueue instead of add_task
services/worker/Dockerfile
```

### Steps
1. arq + Redis (Upstash is sufficient at this scale). One task: `execute_run(run_id)`.
2. Concurrency limit of 3 per worker; one worker to start.
3. Idempotency: `execute_run` claims the run with
   `update runs set status='running' where id=$1 and status='queued' returning *`. No row returned
   means another worker has it — return immediately. This is what makes retries safe.
4. Startup sweep re-enqueues runs stuck in `queued`, and fails runs stuck in `running` past 30
   minutes with a stale-run message.
5. Graceful shutdown: finish the current node, checkpoint, requeue the remainder.

### Tests
- A killed worker mid-run has the run picked up and completed by another.
- Double-enqueue executes once (the claim test).
- The SSE contract is unchanged — RG-032's tests pass without modification.

### Definition of done
Three tests green; RG-032's suite untouched and passing.

### Out of scope
Multi-region workers, priority queues.

Title: RG-053 — Migrate v1 data into v2
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** v1 has a real history on disk: applications under `companies/<company>/<role>/` with
`JD.txt`, `hamsa_resume.tex`, `cover_letter.tex`, `review.json`, `application_status.json`, and
PDFs — plus a curated `source_of_truth.txt` and ten templates. None of it should be retyped.

**User story.** As the v1 user I run one command and my entire history appears in v2 with its
scores and statuses intact.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every v1 application directory becomes an application with a run carrying its original scores.
- The source of truth is imported as structured rows, and the rendered output matches the
  original file.
- Migration is idempotent — running it twice does not duplicate anything.
- A dry-run reports exactly what would be created, and changes nothing.

## Technical plan

### Files
```
apps/api/scripts/migrate_v1.py         --source <path> --user-email <e> [--dry-run]
apps/api/scripts/parsers/v1_sot.py     source_of_truth.txt → structured rows
apps/api/tests/test_migrate_v1.py
```

### Steps
1. **Source of truth.** Parse `base/source_of_truth.txt` into companies, projects, bullets, and
   skills. Then verify by rendering it back with `sot_render` (RG-020) and diffing against the
   original. Report the diff and abort if it is not empty — a lossy career-record import is worse
   than no import.
2. **Templates.** Import `single_page/*.tex` and `multi_page/*.tex` as user-owned rows if they
   differ from the seeded system versions; skip if identical by hash.
3. **Applications.** Walk `companies/**`, using `storage.list_saved_applications()`'s own
   discovery rules — including its fallback globs for oddly-named `.tex` files, which encode real
   history. For each: create the application from the directory slugs and `JD.txt`; create a run
   with `status='succeeded'`; map `review.json` field-for-field onto the `runs` columns (the keys
   already match, per RG-002); upload the `.tex` and PDF files as `documents`; apply
   `application_status.json` to the application's status fields.
4. **Idempotency.** Key on `(user_id, company_slug, role_slug, original_dir)`; skip existing. Store
   `original_dir` in a `migrated_from` column added by this ticket's migration.
5. `--dry-run` prints a table of what would be created and touches nothing.
6. Where `review.json` is missing, create the application with no run rather than skipping it —
   the JD and the `.tex` are still worth having.

### Reuse from v1
`storage.list_saved_applications`, `read_application_status`, and `default_application_status` —
port them into the script as the discovery layer. They already handle the messy real-world cases.

### Tests
- Against a fixture tree of five applications: five applications, five runs, correct scores.
- A second run of the migration creates nothing new.
- `--dry-run` writes nothing and reports the right counts.
- The source-of-truth round-trip diff is empty for the real `source_of_truth.txt`.
- A directory missing `review.json` still produces an application.

### Definition of done
Five tests green; the real v1 tree migrates cleanly end to end.

### Out of scope
Migrating LinkedIn notes or the `ats-checker` cache.

Title: RG-054 — Promote to cloud environments
Description:
## Product requirement

**Problem.** Everything up to here runs locally. Going to the cloud is where a working project
quietly acquires a production incident: a leaked service-role key, an unrestricted CORS origin,
a database with no backups, or a LaTeX container reachable from the internet.

**Outcome.** Two real environments — staging and production — that deploy on merge, hold their
secrets properly, and can be restored after a mistake.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Merging to `main` deploys to staging automatically; production is a manual promotion.
- No secret exists in the repository, in a build log, or in a client bundle.
- The LaTeX service is reachable only from the API, never from the internet.
- The database has automated backups and a rehearsed restore.
- A bad deploy can be rolled back in under five minutes.

## Technical plan

### Topology

| Component | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web | Vercel | Preview per PR, staging on `main`, production on promotion |
| API | Fly.io app `rg-api` | Public, behind HTTPS, 2 machines minimum in production |
| LaTeX | Fly.io app `rg-latex` | **No public IP.** Private 6PN networking only |
| Worker | Fly.io app `rg-worker` | Only if RG-052 has fired |
| Postgres + Storage + Auth | Supabase | One project per environment, never shared |
| Redis | Upstash | Only if RG-052 has fired |

### Files
```
.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
.github/workflows/deploy-production.yml     manual dispatch + environment approval
fly.api.toml  fly.latex.toml  fly.worker.toml
infra/README.md                             runbook: deploy, rollback, restore, rotate
infra/checklist-go-live.md
```

### Steps
1. **Environments.** `staging` and `production` as GitHub Environments, production requiring a
   manual approval. Each holds its own secret set. `.env.example` remains the canonical list of
   names; no environment may define a name absent from it (assert in CI).
2. **Secret discipline.** The Supabase **service-role key exists only in the API's secret store** —
   never in Vercel, never in a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable, never in a preview environment. Add a CI
   check that greps the built web bundle for the service-role prefix and for any `sk-` string, and
   fails the build on a hit.
3. **Network.** `rg-latex` gets no public IP; the API reaches it over `rg-latex.internal`.
   API CORS allows exactly the web origins for that environment — no wildcard, in any environment.
   Supabase RLS is verified against staging by running the RG-002 pgTAP suite post-deploy.
4. **Migrations.** Applied by the deploy job before the new API version starts, and required to be
   backward-compatible with the previous release so a rollback does not need a down-migration.
   Expand-then-contract: add a column in one release, stop reading the old one in the next.
5. **Backups.** Supabase daily backups plus point-in-time recovery on production. A restore is
   **rehearsed once into staging** as part of this ticket — an untested backup is not a backup.
6. **Health and rollback.** `/v1/health` drives Fly's checks; a failing deploy does not take
   traffic. Rollback is `fly releases rollback` for the API and a Vercel instant rollback for the
   web, both written into `infra/README.md` with the exact commands.
7. **Cost and limits.** Set a Fly hard scale cap and a Supabase spend cap. A runaway loop should
   fail, not bill.
8. **Go-live checklist** (`infra/checklist-go-live.md`), all items verified before the first
   production promotion: custom domain and TLS, OAuth redirect URLs for the production origin,
   `allowed_emails` seeded, Sentry receiving from both apps, backups confirmed, restore rehearsed,
   secret-scan check green, rate limits on the public interest endpoint, LaTeX container confirmed
   unreachable from the internet.

### Tests
- Staging deploy is green end to end, and a smoke test signs in and completes a fake-mode run.
- The secret-scan CI check fails against a branch that deliberately leaks a key, then is reverted.
- `rg-latex` is unreachable from a public IP (assert from a runner outside the private network).
- A staging restore from backup produces the expected row counts.
- A rollback returns the previous version within five minutes, timed and recorded in the runbook.

### Definition of done
Five checks recorded in `infra/README.md` with dates; the go-live checklist fully ticked.

### Out of scope
Multi-region, autoscaling policy, SOC2-style compliance work.
